Hello [~accountid:712020:9e0b784a-6c4f-484c-ae35-3356ae04ddf1], the rider responded in [new ticket|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/381661750]:

_“Subject: Re: Formal Apology and Commitment to Resolution Hi Bolt,_

_I am writing to follow up on my recent communication regarding the Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) I submitted. Thank you for your response dated 8 April 2024._

_However, I must express my serious concerns regarding the handling of my request and the subsequent revelation of information that indicates non-compliance with GDPR regulations._

_In your recent email, you stated that the Audio Trip Recordings feature is not available in the United Kingdom and, therefore, no such data was obtained._

_This response has now been contradicted by the attachment of a transcript from the phone conversation between me and Bolt’s Customer Support Team manager on 13 January 2024. I'd like to also emphasise that the transcript requested was for the conversation made on the 12th of April between myself the customer service representatives (not the manager)._

_This suggests that such data does exist and was initially withheld, which raises serious concerns about transparency and compliance with GDPR requirements._

_Under the UK GDPR, I am entitled to access all personal data held about me, including any call recordings that pertain to my interactions with Bolt._

_The initial claim that no such data was available appears to have been a misrepresentation of the facts. This has not only caused significant inconvenience but has also led me to question the integrity of Bolt's data management and customer service practices._

_To address this matter, I formally request the following actions:_

_1*. Immediate Clarification*: An explanation as to why the existence of the call recording was initially denied._

# _Comprehensive Data Access: Provision of all data held about me, including but not limited to call recordings, emails, and any internal notes or communications._
# _Formal Apology: A formal acknowledgment of the oversight and an assurance of steps being taken to prevent such occurrences in the future._
# _GDPR Compliance Review: Confirmation that Bolt will review its compliance with GDPR, specifically concerning the handling and disclosure of personal data._

_Given the gravity of this situation and Bolt’s apparent non-compliance with GDPR, I am left with no choice but to escalate this complaint to the Information Commissioner’s Office (ICO). I will be submitting a formal complaint to the ICO detailing this incident and Bolt’s handling of my DSAR._

_I trust that Bolt will take these concerns seriously and act promptly to rectify the situation. Your swift and thorough response to this complaint will be appreciated and will be considered during the ICO's investigation._

_Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your prompt response and resolution._

_Yours sincerely,_

_Abu”_

Maybe a bit naive, but worked in other companies:

* only AP team can know if something is recoverable or not when looking at invoice. system would not be able to guess it unless entire entity is not registered with VAT (not tax liable)
* AP team changing VAT field to NO-VAT and add amount into main cost



I don’t see why would we assign any tax attribute to tax which we can’t recover and need to absorb the cost. In all downstream reporting it will be showing as NO VAT in any case. So giving right input at source Telema (and later WD invoice approval flow) should be the best IMO. If we start creating another flags or IF/THEN with myriads of TA codes - it will just make life more complex.

*Existing approach:*
AP just put all the total as net amount and 0% VAT.
So we change the data and put the wrong tax code on the invoice. Impact:

* Wrong data in SAF-T, no compliance with supplier's data (both SAF-T and e-invoicing) in tax authority portal
* Not all countries allow zero invoices to be excluded from the tax return. Sometimes we have to declare ALL invoices, it doesn't matter if they are exempt or zero). So there are also compliance issues with tax returns.
* Bolt management are struggling to calculate the amount of non-recoverable VAT they really want to see (that's the strong request).

Hi team, any update about this case?

I’ve quickly checked EE, UK tax rules. If the input tax is not recoverable - it is not an input tax. It is just an ordinary cost. We might have 3 major cases:

* entirely unrecoverable income tax
* specific costs from which tax can’t be recovered
* proportional recovery

in (1) and (2) such invoices will just be treated as cost for full amount - base + tax and you don’t need to report it (usually). tax authorities usually care only about invoices which are claimed for recovery. those should not exceed invoices reported by supplier as taxable income.

Let’s check some SAFT examples - gut feel says that those will have same logic as for EE UK example - no input vat (by law) - not reported.

Proportional recovery will always be in VAT adjustments as it can be determined only after month ended and you know your split of taxable/non-taxable revenue. Invoices will be declared / accounted as is.

🤔 So having no vat invoice should in theory be well compliant with SAF-T. If you don’t claim back - government is happy.



Those are not 0% - those are NO-VAT cases. 0% should be definitely reported both sales and purchase.



Re visibility - let’s have a deeper example. Usually you would be interested in knowing $ of un-recovered vat only for use case 3. for 1 and 2 this is just a cost and should be budgeted with VAT in mind. If service is 100 and 20 vat on top, but you know that you can’t recover - you always budget 120 as a cost of type X. There (in theory) should not be tangible value to distinguish cases when service costed 120 because you can’t recover OR because supply is not taxable and just cost is 120. Let’s figure out what conclusions and(or) management decisions would be made based on the knowledge of un-recover-ability of vat for cases (1) and (2) and why would we need this non-typical complexity.



For intercompany cases - unrecoverable VAT is a separate thing. as by default IC transaction could be indirect tax neutral or revenue-cost neutral segregation of unrecoverable indirect tax is beneficial. Same will come from IC elimination during consolidation. And to simplify this - companies might post:

*Dr IC cost 100* + Dr IC Unrecoverable tax 20   / Cr IC Payable 120

Dr IC Receivable 120 / Cr *IC Revenue 100* Cr TaxPayable 20

to simplify analysis for IC eliminations you benefit from excluding of such tax during cost recognition so that your elimination of revenue + cost == 0

_Hi_ [~accountid:610a3ee66051c5006aeeeea1] _I agree with DLA and think we have here a balanced solution - what do you think?_



*BACKGROUND*

* One of the reclassification criteria in Portugal for platform workers is the exercise by the platform of labour powers, namely disciplinary power, including exclusion from future activities on the platform through account deactivation. Blocking may be therefore a reclassification criteria.
* Therefore in 2023 the internal decision was made that all automatic or statistical blocking (linked to Driver Score & Acceptance Rate) should been removed. It is no longer possible to ask a driver to retrain. The only blocking still happening relates to lack of mandatory documents, safety incidents or fraud - though a more cautious approach has been adopted there and relevant communication should be made to the fleet operators and the drivers to give them notice (when possible) and relevant explanation.
* A few months ago we implemented in PT a warning / block process for FR (finish rate) which was based on the following criteria: (a) *the driver accepts the ride*; (b) *the driver then cancels the ride* for no reason, or states it as arrived to the location and passenger is not there (when that is not the case due to geo-location review). This scenario seems to be a fraud since the driver is defrauding the expectations of the passenger and it also seems to be against the TVDE law. Consequently, it would follow under the fraud and compliance blocking reasons.

*PROPOSED PROCESS*

* Under this proposed new process Bolt would issue a warning everytime that a driver is recurrently rejecting rides. After the third consecutive warning we consider a 1 week temporary block. The process would be run by the local team and considering 30%+ rejection of rides.

*LEGAL REVIEW*

*A) Risks with the proposed process: regulatory and reclassification*

The freedom to accept or refuse the ride is a relevant sign of autonomy and independence and a very relevant factor to prevent reclassification, as the possibility of refusing to work may be seen as setting legal subordination aside. Thus, the implementation of a system where the driver is restricted in his/her freedom to accept or refuse the ride may be considered a sign of legal subordination, specifically the one provided for in paragraph d) of Article 12-A of the Labour Code – “_restriction of the activity provider's autonomy with regard to the organisation of work, especially with respect to_ [...] _the possibility of accepting or refusing tasks_, [...] _through the application of sanctions_”.  Overall, this process would be detrimental to Bolt in reclassification claims and would, according to the HQ analysis', potentially impact the ability to defend the currently model in -45%.

The freedom to accept or refuse the ride is also established in Clause 1.12 of the T&Cs applicable to TVDE operators.

In our opinion Article 8(1) of the TVDE law aims at guaranteeing access to ride-hailing services for all people, preventing refusals based on random factors. We understand this interpretation to be consistent with the wording of Article 7, under which the users shall not be refused on grounds of discriminatory factors such as age or nationality. The combined interpretation of these two provisions leads to the conclusion that TVDE services must be universally accessible to all users, as a principle, as only under exceptional and limited situations it can be legitimately refused.

As regards the implementation of the proposed new process, the reasons to issue warnings and temporarily block drivers does not seem to be necessarily linked to guaranteeing access to the service, but rather to ensuring speed in the ride’s allocation process. However, we consider that the implementation of a sanction imposed by Bolt to the drivers (suspension or blocking) merely based on quantitative factors such as the number or percentage of refusals, without any link to non-compliance with Article 8 of the TVDE law, is likely to create a risk of reclassification, as described above.

*B ) Mitigation solutions*

Below recommendations to consider in order to mitigate the risks described above:

* *Amend the T&Cs* applicable to TVDE/Taxi operators by including a presumption that if drivers refuse 30%+ of ride services, they are not compliant with Article 8 of the TVDE law. This presumption would be based on criteria of reasonableness, in that it is not likely that more than 30% of rides, in a given period, are refused on the basis of the factors listed in Article 8. This presumption would not eliminate the risk of reclassification, but in our opinion would mitigate it.
* The *comms* should include justification related to compliance with legal obligations:
** In the case of TVDE:  Article 14(2) of the TVDE law, under which Bolt shall block access to the services provided by the platform by TVDE operators, drivers or vehicles that fail to comply with any of the requirements referred to in this law, whenever it is or should be aware of it.
** In the case of Taxi: Article 24(3) of the Taxi law
* The operator or driver would have to be given the opportunity to *appeal* the decision namely by rebuting the presumption and therefore demonstrate that the refusals above 30% were actually made on the basis of Article 8.

We already have editable centralized release freeze calendar in Builder available at [http://unicorn-builder.internal/builder-ui/release-freezes|http://unicorn-builder.internal/builder-ui/release-freezes]

Currently there is no {{type}} of release freeze, so every entry is actually a {{ReleaseFreeze}}. Builder has implemented a pipeline step that fails the whole release if it is being made within any active ReleaseFree interval.

ReleaseFreeze currently has {{Application}} level granularity. Meaning its possible to mark which {{Applications}} are affected by a {{ReleaseFreeze}}.

h2. *New Interval Types:*

To support other types of time intervals - we need to introduce additional indicative field to {{release_freeze}} table, AND where we have the release freeze checks (in a special step of a pipeline), we need to introduce appropriate code logic handling these new types:

* {{ReleaseFreeze}} type - when inside interval: prevent from releasing (currently already supported)
* {{HighDemand}} type - when inside interval: warn about high demand period, but allow release after confirmation
* {{AdvisedRelease}} type - when outside of interval: warn that current time is outside of advised release interval, but allow release after confirmation

We also need to have definitions and clarifications: 

* What is High Demand interval (e.g. a time interval outside Release Freeze when we expect high load on our services? for which vertical? in a specific country? etc)
* What is AdvisedRelease interval (Supposedly it is working hours? For which vertical? which timezone? etc.)
* Does it makes sense to introduce {{Package}} or {{Vertical}} level granularity? For example {{HighDemand}} might only be related to {{Delivery}} vertical, but not for others? Currently, release has information of packages being released. Mapping them to {{Verticals}} has to be introduced.

h2. Incidents Integration:

Need to clarify what is the source of truth for incidents. Is it possible to query for active incidents (edit: we don't have centralized db for incidents), or we have to tackle them somehow differently (edit: we can extend slack zappier script so it could call webhook when incident is open/resolved). Whenever we have release freeze checks (in a special step of a pipeline), we can additionally verify that there is an open incident:

* Open Incident  - warn that currently there’s ongoing *matching* incident, but allow release after confirmation

In a simplified approach, any open incident can be matched, in an advanced scenario - every incident has indication of affected {{Vertical}}. This references the need to have a mapping between release and a {{Vertical}} to support graceful matching relevant incidents.

Interesują nas dwie kategorie: 

* do 200 m^2^ – musi przynajmniej *pobierać kaucję* i zawrzeć umowę *z podmiotem reprezentującym.* Udział w systemie kaucyjnym w pełnym zakresie (pobieranie/zwracanie kaucji, zbiórka opakowań/odpadów opakowaniowych) jest dobrowolny.
* ponad 200 m^2^ – *obowiązkowy* udział w systemie kaucyjnym (pobieranie/zwracanie kaucji, zbiórka opakowań/odpadów opakowaniowych).

Jako że powierzchnia naszych magazynów nie przekracza 200 m^2^ możemy przyjąć, że drugi punkt nas nie dotyczy.

Zostaje natomiast kategoria 1, zgodnie z którą: “Przedsiębiorca prowadzący jednostkę handlu detalicznego lub hurtowego o powierzchni sprzedaży nie większej niż 200 m2, w której użytkownikom końcowym są oferowane produkty będące napojami w opakowaniach na napoje objętych systemem kaucyjnym, *jest obowiązany uczestniczyć w systemie kaucyjnym w zakresie co najmniej pobierania kaucji* oraz może uczestniczyć w tym systemie w zakresie zwracania kaucji oraz zbierania pustych opakowań i odpadów opakowaniowych.”

Argumentem na naszą korzyść jest fakt, że nasze magazyny nie stanowią ogólnodostępnej powierzchni obiektu handlowego, jednak wydaje się, że intencją ustawodawcy było objęcie regulacją wszystkich opakowań. Na ten moment nie ma jeszcze orzecznictwa ani komentarzy prawnych dotyczących tej kwestii. 

*sankcja:* kto wbrew przepisowi art. 44 ust. 1, prowadząc jednostkę handlu detalicznego lub hurtowego o powierzchni sprzedaży nie większej niż 200 m^2^, w której użytkownikom końcowym są oferowane produkty będące napojami w opakowaniach na napoje objętych systemem kaucyjnym, nie pobiera kaucji podlega każe administracyjnej od 10 000 zł do 500 000 zł;

Hi [~accountid:712020:46da73ea-bcbb-4b69-8e3e-ac27402d61bc] and [~accountid:712020:ab95f96b-73f1-4bb8-a5fd-5178ef3f1339] please see below our feedback on this new project:

*BACKGROUND*

* One of the reclassification criteria in Portugal for platform workers is the exercise by the platform of labour powers, namely disciplinary power, including exclusion from future activities on the platform through account deactivation. Blocking may be therefore a reclassification criteria.
* Therefore in 2023 the internal decision was made that all automatic or statistical blocking (linked to Driver Score & Acceptance Rate) should been removed. It is no longer possible to ask a driver to retrain. The only blocking still happening relates to lack of mandatory documents, safety incidents or fraud - though a more cautious approach has been adopted there and relevant communication should be made to the fleet operators and the drivers to give them notice (when possible) and relevant explanation.
* A few months ago we implemented in PT a warning / block process for FR (finish rate) which was based on the following criteria: (a) *the driver accepts the ride*; (b) *the driver then cancels the ride* for no reason, or states it as arrived to the location and passenger is not there (when that is not the case due to geo-location review). This scenario seems to be a fraud since the driver is defrauding the expectations of the passenger and it also seems to be against the TVDE law. Consequently, it would follow under the fraud and compliance blocking reasons.

*PROPOSED PROCESS*

* Under this proposed new process Bolt would issue a warning everytime that a driver is recurrently rejecting rides. After the third consecutive warning we consider a 1 week temporary block. The process would be run by the local team and considering 30%+ rejection of rides.

*LEGAL REVIEW*

*A) Risks with the proposed process: regulatory and reclassification*

The freedom to accept or refuse the ride is a relevant sign of autonomy and independence and a very relevant factor to prevent reclassification, as the possibility of refusing to work may be seen as setting legal subordination aside. Thus, the implementation of a system where the driver is restricted in his/her freedom to accept or refuse the ride may be considered a sign of legal subordination, specifically the one provided for in paragraph d) of Article 12-A of the Labour Code – “_restriction of the activity provider's autonomy with regard to the organisation of work, especially with respect to_ [...] _the possibility of accepting or refusing tasks_, [...] _through the application of sanctions_”. Overall, this process would be detrimental to Bolt in reclassification claims and would, according to the HQ analysis', potentially impact the ability to defend the currently model in -45%.

The freedom to accept or refuse the ride is also established in Clause 1.12 of the T&Cs applicable to TVDE operators.

In our opinion Article 8(1) of the TVDE law aims at guaranteeing access to ride-hailing services for all people, preventing refusals based on random factors. We understand this interpretation to be consistent with the wording of Article 7, under which the users shall not be refused on grounds of discriminatory factors such as age or nationality. The combined interpretation of these two provisions leads to the conclusion that TVDE services must be universally accessible to all users, as a principle, as only under exceptional and limited situations it can be legitimately refused.

As regards the implementation of the proposed new process, the reasons to issue warnings and temporarily block drivers does not seem to be necessarily linked to guaranteeing access to the service, but rather to ensuring speed in the ride’s allocation process. However, we consider that the implementation of a sanction imposed by Bolt to the drivers (suspension or blocking) merely based on quantitative factors such as the number or percentage of refusals, without any link to non-compliance with Article 8 of the TVDE law, is likely to create a risk of reclassification, as described above.

*B ) Mitigation solutions*

Below recommendations to consider in order to mitigate the risks described above:

* *Amend the T&Cs* applicable to TVDE/Taxi operators by including a presumption that if drivers refuse 30%+ of ride services, they are not compliant with Article 8 of the TVDE law. This presumption would be based on criteria of reasonableness, in that it is not likely that more than 30% of rides, in a given period, are refused on the basis of the factors listed in Article 8. This presumption would not eliminate the risk of reclassification, but in our opinion would mitigate it.
* The *comms* should include justification related to compliance with legal obligations:
** In the case of TVDE: Article 14(2) of the TVDE law, under which Bolt shall block access to the services provided by the platform by TVDE operators, drivers or vehicles that fail to comply with any of the requirements referred to in this law, whenever it is or should be aware of it.
** In the case of Taxi: Article 24(3) of the Taxi law
* The operator or driver would have to be given the opportunity to *appeal* the decision namely by rebuting the presumption and therefore demonstrate that the refusals above 30% were actually made on the basis of Article 8.

Hey Adam 🙂 

_But how can we know that some driver was HBed when he asked in the past for deletion and so we should not have more any informations about him?_

The old deleted/hidden accounts will be visible in the duplicates view, hence visible to the Supply team. The driver account status does not affect the visibility in the Admin registration. Admin system won’t automatically reject the registration just because at some point, the driver was deleted. It will, however, trigger a duplicate. Whatever you do with the driver profile, the driver is never „blocked“ from new registration attempts, unless your supply team would filter out the „Is duplicate“ in the Driver Registrations search. 

You could completely erase the driver from Admin only if you also delete the phone number, and remove the username and email. Only in this case, this partner will not affect future registration attempts and the new application will appear as „from scratch“.

Hi, [~accountid:5bed9c4bbd55fc123dda10b9]! I am coming back after receiving the full feedback from the external counsel to share with you the issues that are currently blocking us from proceeding. Please review and let me know what do you think.

Issues:

* Drivers need to have a licence "Road and motor transport - cargo transport operated by vehicles of a maximum authorised weight not exceeding 3.5 tonnes" to provide services under Bolt Send. Bolt needs to make sure that only Drivers with the appropriate licence have access to this category.
** The procedure for obtaining this licence is relatively simple. The trade license is granted essentially automatically. There is no need to provide any documentation, just submit an application to the trade office. The office will forward the application to the Department of Transportation and if the applicant has no criminal record related to this scope of business, the office will issue the license within 30 days. Usually is the license issued within two weeks. If the drivers are employees of a company (fleet) that has a trade licence, then they do not have to arrange it themselves (similar to ride-hailing).
* It is not possible to limit Driver's liability as per clause 2.10 of the T&Cs. Drivers that will opt into Bolt Send category will bear the full liability in case the parcel is lost or damaged.
* Undelivered parcels will not be accepted by the police. Lost items are normally passed to municipality, but since parcel is not lost and the owner is known, municipality will not accept parcels. We need to come up with a different solution. The best solution from Bolt's perspective would be if the driver would take the parcel for safe keeping or take it to the fleet's office/specified location so as the driver or the fleet would be responsible for the safe keeping of the parcel. We need to try to avoid handling undelivered parcels ourselves to reduce our risks.
* It is recommended by the external counsel for Bolt to obtain freight forwarding licence („Freight forwarding and representation in customs proceedings“) to operate Bolt Send. Our competitor providing similar service (Liftago) has this licence. This is recommended because our activity would be borderline between service brokering (we have this trade licence) and freight forwarding (we do not have this trade licence).
** We would need to apply for a trade licence from the trade licensing office and also add reference to this trade to Bolt's information on the commercial register, which requires a visit to a notary and amendment of articles of association.
* No specific documents are required to be in possession of the Driver during the provision of the service, however, the law prescribes that the Driver has the right to request confirmation of the transport order and the sender can request confirmation of the receipt of the parcel by the Driver. Such confirmations shall be in writing, therefore, our app needs to have this information - details of the order and confirmation that the parcel was received by the Driver.
* We need to specify that the service is available only within the territory of Czech Republic.

{color:#bf2600}_Do you see any blockers to using the existing identification metric/naming in our system? For drivers, we’d like to use the driver IDs as their names on the landing page. As for Fleets, can we use their real Fleet names?_{color}

From data protection POV:

* as for the Fleets, I do not see a problem here - we just must make sure that we have the right to use any IP (trademarks, etc) if we decide to. 
* as for the drivers, if we want to ensure the data is pseudonymised (as we agreed prior), we must make sure that only the driver can understand their score on the website (and relevant Bolt employees). Because of this, I ideally I would prefer to replace driver ID with some made up identifier .

*Duplicating my responses from Slack*: at least for drivers, they ideally must be able to opt out at any time. Technical difficulties to implement opt out are not a valid reason not to provide opt out options.

*Also, opt out to unsubscribe from emails must be available for all emails that driver/fleet are receiving.* 

We can definitely avoid opt-out *if* we make the enrolment opt-in based - i.e. if the driver/fleet received the emails and actively chose to participate.

If it's technically difficult to provide opt-out, I would advise to make the campaign *opt-in* based.

If we do not do it, I would say the risks are limited as there are no negative consequences for driver/fleet except for possibly perceived email spam that they cannot effectively stop.

*FYI: Email from Ferdy at Sackers re Pension and Interest Payments:*

Dear Iva

No problem on the follow up email.   We’ve brought together your questions in one email response below.

*The likelihood of TPR requesting that Bolt pays interest on any backdated contributions (BDCs)*

# As noted in my earlier email, if at some point in the future TPR were to issue a Compliance Notice or Unpaid Contributions Notice, it has a discretion whether to also impose a requirement to pay interest at the specified rate.
# In deciding whether to do so, TPR should take into account all relevant factors.
# We expect an important factor will be ‘restoration’ ie one of TPR’s stated compliance outcomes aimed at restoring workers to the position they would have been in with regard to contributions to their pension scheme, had no breach occurred.
# We cannot give a %age likelihood of TPR imposing a requirement to pay interest at the specified rate because we do not have any first hand experience of TPR exercising that power nor are we aware of any publicly available statistics in this regard.
# But given TPR’s stated compliance aims, we think it is at least more likely than not.

*Are there are any mitigation strategies that Bolt could employ to minimize risks of a requirement to pay interest being imposed?*

# A mitigation strategy that we have experience of is making a compensation proposal to TPR before it issues a Compliance Notice or Unpaid Contributions Notice.
# Should TPR be satisfied with both (1) the proposal itself and (2) that it has been robustly implemented, TPR is unlikely then to issue (and, in our experience, has never issued) a Compliance Notice or Unpaid Contributions Notice.  Clearly if neither notice is issued, then a requirement to pay interest would not arise.
# A compensation proposal may specify a lower rate of interest than the specified rate of interest under the legislation.  Although there is not one right rate or approach, in our experience, a common approach is to propose a rate that is broadly equivalent to the investment returns that a worker would have received in a typical default fund over the period in question. 

*Our opinion on what would be a ‘backstop’ date for Bolt and why*

# In the same way as outlined in relation to the question on interest above, if at some point in the future TPR were to issue a Compliance Notice or Unpaid Contributions Notice, its compliance outcome of restoration is likely to be engaged.
# With this in mind, we would expect TPR’s starting point to be to enforce from the point that non-compliance with any automatic enrolment duties began – that is, without the application of a ‘backstop’.
# However, were a compensation proposal to be made to TPR that included a ‘backstop’, we think TPR might in principle be prepared to accept this, provided the ‘backstop’ is justified on the basis of proportionality.  We suspect that TPR may approach this in the same way it recognises that they are circumstances in which it may not be appropriate to enforce in relation to workers who have since left employment (in a more traditional employment model).
# In putting forward a backstop date, our advice would be not to propose an arbitrary period of time - for example, 6 years.  There should be some rationale regarding the number of drivers covered by the period earlier than the proposed backstop date, the robustness of the payroll records before then, and the amount of work / cost involved in going back to an earlier date.
# We don’t have any direct experience of seeking to agree a ‘backstop’ with TPR but it may be that it is in circumstances of putting forward a compensation proposal that Deloitte have come across this. If Deloitte are able to provide more information, we would be happy to comment further.
# What we would say at this stage is that any proposal for a ‘backstop’ date would be highly fact-specific and would need to be considered in the context of the full terms of any compensation proposal.

I am sharing with you an update regarding tool amendments. I have prepared a draft [here|https://www.cognitoforms.com/taxify1/globaleventassessmenttoolamendmentsdraft/build], you need to be logged in to Cognito to access a “Preview” mode. It allows you to see the mock-up and submit test forms without actually submitting anything or triggering notifications. The “Preview” button can be found in the top right corner.

* Once the Assessment is closed, the form has the status {{Finalised}}. No fields can be edited in that state. I added the button {{Re-open (Edit)}}, which will erase {{Yes}} response to *Has The Assessment Been Completed?* question, and push the form to the “Re-opened” state, making it editable upon reopening. 
* When changes are made to the form, it will need to be closed again, and the reasoning for amendment provided. This is done by choosing {{Yes}} to *Has The Assessment Been Completed?* again, and click the {{Amend}} button.
* Then, the form is pushed to the {{Amended}} state. The amended form doesn't trigger notifications and can be re-opened and edited again.

Currently, only Rides have this functionality, and only certain fields can be edited. This setup allows amendments for all business lines and all fields.

1. One important thing is that re-opening will not return the entry to the Event Dashboard sheet. -Meaning, that if the form is re-opened and not finalised right after — it will be lost foreve-r… To avoid “hanging” forms I suggest we have a Looker overview. The data is synced daily, which should be sufficient to highlight if there are any “lost” cases.

2. Another important question is regarding triggering workflows. Sometimes, it would make sense to trigger the notifications again. For example, in the case of the UK team. We could still highlight that those are sent from the Amendment stage (and might require some attention as to potential duplicates). We could offer 2 options, one would allow to {{Finalise}}, and run all the related flows. And another would only {{Amend}} the case details, without triggering any workflows.

3. This might look a bit different for High and Significant UK/IE as a result of Investigation removal. The logic will stay.

{quote}The Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 (SCD Type 2) data structure in a data warehouse is specifically designed to manage and store historical data changes over time, ensuring that the full history of these changes is captured. This is achieved through the use of History Tables, which are immutable and are either built or backfilled with SCD2 tables. These tables maintain the history of all dimensions with date-level granularity, which is essential for reproducing historical metrics based on the state of dimensions at the time an event occurred. This approach not only allows for accurate historical analysis and decision-making but also supports trend analysis, auditing, and other forms of historical scrutiny by ensuring that all changes are meticulously recorded and accessible.

The same principles apply to LV and LT also.

Re-opening this ticket due to latest developments (when Legal found out that Ops was about to launch this green Tesla project) - Copying here the advice provided in the channel #temp-ev-pt:

_[17 May 2024]_

The advice was provided in Feb and the conclusion was that this would *likely be against the TVDE law since there is a general prohibition of publicity and also the principle that RH vehicles should be uncharacterised*. Using the Bolt green would arguably be against the regulations and lead to fines.

Depending on the seriousness of the offence committed, an *accessory sanction of being banned from exercising the activity for a maximum period of two years may be applied* for the offences provided under the TVDE law.

_[23 May 2024]_

Please see below the Legal assessment provided by outside attorney (DLA). Let me know if you have any questions and want to further discuss! While the outside attorney cannot assess the risks precisely in terms of percentage, below please find a list of the *potential risks arising from the proposed green Tesla project* and general level of risk:

* The TVDE regime prohibits the display of brands and advertising on TVDE vehicles, as these must be uncharacterized. On the other hand, the concept of advertising in Portuguese law is significantly wide. In view of the above, we cannot exclude the *possibility that the color of the vehicles, in itself, falls within the concept of advertising* and, consequently, Bolt can be subject to the sanctions provided for on the TVDE legal regime: (i) *payment of a fine of € 5.000 to € 15.000* and (ii) *ban on the exercise of the activity for a maximum period of two years*. However, the outside attorney estimates this risk as *less than 50%*, namely for the following reasons: (i) there is no other reference to the Bolt brand on the vehicles and (ii) the color is not registered as a Bolt trademark.

* We maintain the risk assessment previously carried out in relation to the *cooperation agreements*:

* In terms of *ride-hailing regulatory risks*, as you know, the TVDE regime prohibits electronic platforms to own TVDE vehicles, or finance or be an interested party in business relating to the acquisition, rental, leasing or other use of TVDE vehicles --> *Bolt's contribution to the purchase of vehicles by the FO is therefore likely to involve a regulatory risk*. The penalty for the *administrative liability ranges between €5,000 and €15,000*, depending on the degree of fault.
* The *decision to interdict activity* is highly dependant on the level of risk that is taken by Bolt. We have no knowledge about prior cases where these measures were applied. Although we cannot exclude the possibility of such measures being applied to Bolt, we understand that this prohibition mainly aims to protect the integrity of the TVDE services and was not thought for the situations as the one in this case. As such, we believe that it is *unlikely* that this deal will create *significant risks* for Bolt as regards the application of any of these measures.
* From a *banking regulatory perspective*, it is *unlikely* that the envisaged agreement with the FOs will be deemed as being in violation of the principle of banking monopoly, because the contribution from Bolt to the FO does not match the characteristics of a professional lending activity, namely it (i) does not correspond to the professional activity of Bolt, (ii) does not include an interest on the principal amount, and (iii) the return on investment is directly linked to growth of business.

* You should also note that both from a banking or ride-hailing regulatory perspective if a penalty is applied to Bolt, the competent authorities may decide to make the *decision public* (e.g. local news).

* Please note that even though this project does not change the risk assessment in relation to the cooperation agreements, *it might trigger investigations and questions from the regulator*. In that case, the regulator will have rights equivalent to authority agents and the *cooperation agreements might have to be disclosed*.

*Things to consider / recommendations from Legal*:

* *gradual roll out* (to see if it attracts the regulator's attention);
* *no public communication / PR on this project* (as this cannot be seen as advertising and we need to ensure this cannot be linked to the cooperation agreements).

Dear Johann Zmiro,

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *19 May 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example,that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* to which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Conversation history*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/|smart-link]  , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data,restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

You will find a .csv file per environment:

* prelive_users_by_schema_24-05-28.csv
* live_users_by_schema_24-05-28.csv

 

The included columns are:

* *cluster*. Database cluster
* *hostgroup*. Database cluster ID
* *type*. Database management system [mysql, tidb]
* *collected_at*. Collection [time.time()|https://docs.python.org/3/library/time.html#time.time]
* *env*. Environment [prelive, live]
* *user*. Database username
* *table_schema*. The database that the user can access. * meaning access to all databases.
* *privilege_type*. Type of privilege that the user has granted.
* *grant_priv*. Does the user have grant privileges [Y/N]
* *locked*. Is the user locked [Y/N]
* *created_at*. Created date for users created by configless.

 

The list of users is obtained by a Python script that iterates through the existent database clusters and collects users from {{mysql.user}} table and _some_ privileges from the {{INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES}} table, [this|https://github.com/bolteu/db-configless/blob/main/configless/meta.py#L114-L139] is the query executed:


{noformat}            SELECT
                mu.User,
                mu.Host,
                COALESCE(sp.TABLE_SCHEMA, "*") AS TABLE_SCHEMA,
                COALESCE(sp.PRIVILEGE_TYPE, "*") AS PRIVILEGE_TYPE,
                mu.Grant_priv AS Grant_priv,
                mu.account_locked AS account_locked
            FROM
                mysql.user mu
            LEFT JOIN
                INFORMATION_SCHEMA.SCHEMA_PRIVILEGES sp ON GRANTEE = CONCAT("'", mu.User, "'", "@", "'", mu.Host, "'");{noformat}

Hey! _Replying here for visibility as we’re still in the progress of establishing best practices globally when it comes to legal support with regards to (increasing number of) b2g sales._

Especially since it's a take-it-or-leave-it then the max Legal can do is highlight the legal risks (inclusion of further subject matter experts e.g. info-sec if needed rests with business) in order for business to make an informed business decision. 

*From Anusha’s quick review of the key legal document, i.e. the framework agreement it's already clear that on several points we’re exposed beyond our standard,* *e.g.* term, termination and unilateral extension rights, being subject to customer’s policies and procedures (we’re not yet aware of, or might not even exist yet), full responsibility for drivers (theoretically very problematic anywhere outside UK from the reclass. perspective), generic yet strict  commitments related to replacing services while acceptance criteria (among other commercial specifics) seem to be undecided for now(?), audit rights all together (see both 16.1 and 20.5), indemnities, liability (if strictly limited to Bolt Business account SaaS then no major issue but if also includes liability for the underlying service providers then def. an issue outside UK).

And indeed at least generic disclosures regarding the ongoing litigation should be made. Also, how and which scope would Non-Employee Vetting Standards External Guidance apply to us? Just Bolt Ops to be checked, or Bolt employees, or drivers(!), or? So the remining docs should be subject to legal sanity check as well.

Principally also specialist tax, privacy and intellectual property counsels should review respective bits though imho would be an overkill (it’s huge deals and take-it-or-leave-it anyway). _This for the time being remains strictly my view as not only other legal counsels but also business itself and management might prefer a more scrutinizing approach._

*So all in all*  [~accountid:5f3f89563e9e2e004dfe49a3] *how do you feel about greenlighting this from the commercial end knowing what you know (and don’t know) based on the above?*
_In reality my bet is that should we be successful in signing them will have a new major riding company  and minimal friction in relation to all the possible risks. But that’s just a bet._

*In each case we need to agree on the way forward for b2g/enterprise sales, because if the expectation from business (and management under the relevant policies) is to conduct a regular legal review of all documentation then we might have a resource issue on the legal side to start with.* 

There might be room for a smart approach though - see the Baltics experience where Sales manages everything on their side (as it’s very standard and the key risks are already calculated in) and reaches out to Legal only with specific questions. TBD whether viable for all stakeholders incl mgmt.

All thoughts most welcome!

Our_ [+_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+|https://bolt.eu/en-th/legal/terms-for-bolt-business/?category=boltBusiness] _Section 4 states explicitly that Bolt and the business customer maintain their independent data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its processing activities and adherence to applicable laws, including the GDPR and the Nigerian Data Protection Act 2023._

_When a business customer`s employee or any data subject uses Bolt Business services for a ride, they are treated as a regular user of the Bolt Rider App. The experience of these business users is identical to that of regular users, except for the availability of an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride). This may result in a scenario where, if a business customer deactivates and removes a business user's account, this individual will lose access to an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride)._

_However, they will continue to be a customer of Bolt, which means Bolt will keep processing their personal data unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention period specified in_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/] _expires. In practical terms, this means that the personal data provided by business customers is  used to match newly added business users with the accounts of standard users. Individuals remain in control over their data._

_Additionally, as there had been a contractual relationship with the business customer, the details of the business rider's account may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from the agreement with the business client. Deleting personal data on the request of business customers may deprive both Bolt and the individual from the opportunity to defend or substantiate their claims in the event that any claims should arise. Therefore, the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller for the above stated purposes unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims) expires, as outlined in the applicable_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/]_._

_Please note that the notion of controllership in our arrangement is analysed by the_ [+_European Data Protection Board (EDPB) Guidelines 07/2020_+|https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en] _on the concepts of controller and processor. Specifically, p. 27 para. 82 demonstrates this via “_*_Example: Taxi service”_*_. While Bolt operates as an online platform rather than providing taxi services directly, the example still effectively clarifies the logic underpinning the controller relationship. {quote}[~accountid:5f2d0e2efa591d0015f85227] an additional question: Is it even possible that an insurer would compensate for damages caused by a user in violation of our T&C and then recourse this amount from Bolt or a business client? I believe the insurer would simply reject the claim.{quote}

The difference between the RGL/PA and MTPL is that RGL/PA is voluntary insurance (so the insurer can reject the compensation to the injured party if the conditions are breached). MTPL, however, is compulsory insurance and heavily regulated, meaning that the injured party must be compensated no matter what first (and later the insurer can figure out how or whether he can recourse the claim from the damaging party).

Let me put it this way. We have a global program that is rolled out differently depending on the risk profile of the individual countries. The program is called “Bolt rewards”.

In high-risk markets, we recommend only offering third-party offers that have a low value (e.g. restaurant or car wash vouchers, fuel cards, etc.). One of the key questions is of course *what the drivers have to do to receive these fuel cards*. 
*Every driver must have the opportunity* to receive these fuel cards. If KPIs are to be used here, then *only finished rides* are permitted. The number of finished rides must *never be so high that the vehicles would effectively be driving exclusively for Bolt*.

“Hello Dominika,

This morning we discovered that BOLT SERVICES RO S.R.L. had unusually large amounts of errors in our system. This had been going on for a couple of days. 

All of them were related to a file type that we call aperak in Telema. These are documents that get sent back from your Workday to Telema's system after Workday has received an invoice from eFlow. When eFlow receives the aperak, then the invoice goes to archived status in eFlow because it knows that your ERP has accepted and processed it. Due to this error some of the invoices were not going to archived status but kept waiting for the aperak.

We looked into it and the reason why this happens is because we tried to correct BOLT SERVICES RO S.R.L. company registration number in Telema's system. The first change of the registration number happened around 20.05.

All of the invoices that were sent to Workday from eFlow before the registration number change went to errors when Workday tried to send aperak back to Telema because the company with that registration number didn't exist in the system anymore. 

Currently we have restored the previous company settings where the registration number is wrong. Now you can send back the signal from Workday to eFlow. 

Our IT department is in contact with your ERP and their Bolt contact. They are trying to schedule a date for the registration code change so minimum number (or none) of documents would be affected by it.

Sorry for the inconvenience and thank you for bringing it up!”

Hello [~accountid:637f26822acfad92d7b13ddb] 

I apologize for the long time to wait for a response, but to understand what the reason for this problem is, sometimes we need more time to investigate. 

Integration refers to the process of transferring data from one system (System A) to another system (System B). According to established best practices and design principles, integration should focus exclusively on data transfer, without altering the data in any way. Manipulating data during integration introduces risks and violates general programming principles and internal controls.

To clarify, any data rounding or manipulation occurs within the source system, Telema, and not during the integration process. The integration, which moves data from Telema (System A) to Workday (System B), has been executed correctly, as the data was transferred successfully.

Integration refers to the process of transferring data from one system (System A) to another system (System B). According to established best practices and design principles, integration should focus exclusively on data transfer, without altering the data in any way. Manipulating data during integration introduces risks and violates general programming principles and internal controls.

To clarify, any data rounding or manipulation occurs within the source system, Telema, and not during the integration process. The integration, which moves data from Telema (System A) to Workday (System B), has been executed correctly, as the data was transferred successfully.

Regarding data accuracy and integrity, the integration process does not perform any checks. Therefore, it is essential that no data calculations, deletions, or creations occur during integration. If discrepancies are found between the data in Workday and Telema, it means that such data discrepancies originated from Telema.

{code:python}#!/usr/bin/env python
import requests
import json
import time

url='http://localhost:9000/backend'
#url='http://localhost:9000/backend-live'

refresh_stuff = {"refresh_token":"8no8RoteLoeT23tETOreoceOSAl………………"}

access_token = ''
last_access_token = 0
common_headers = {}

def update_access_token():
    global access_token
    global common_headers
    global last_access_token

    if time.time() - last_access_token < 60:
        return # no need to update access token yet

    response = requests.post(
        f'{url}/admin-user/adminPanel/getAccessToken',
        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'},
        data=json.dumps(refresh_stuff)
    )
    
    result = response.json()
    access_token = result['data']['access_token']
    common_headers = {
        'Authorization': f'Bearer {access_token}',
        'Content-Type': 'application/json'
    }
    last_access_token = time.time()

update_access_token()

#################### fetch city groups ####################
city_groups = []
city_id_to_city_group = {}
uuid_to_city_group = {}
name_to_city_group = {}

def fetch_city_groups():
    global city_groups
    global city_id_to_city_group
    global uuid_to_city_group

    city_groups = requests.post(f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/list?limit=10000&offset=0', headers=common_headers).json()['data']['results']
    city_id_to_city_group = {}
    uuid_to_city_group = {}

    for city_group in city_groups:
        uuid_to_city_group[city_group['uuid']] = city_group
        if city_group['city_id']:
            city_id_to_city_group[city_group['city_id']] = city_group
        else:
            name_to_city_group[city_group['name']] = city_group

fetch_city_groups()

#response = requests.post(
#    f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/fetch',
#    headers=common_headers,
#    data=json.dumps({"uuid": "9befd948-5884-45e6-b8fc-1e15b98ad304"})
#)
#print(response.json())

#################### fetch cities ####################

cities = requests.get(f'{url}/system-data-admin/adminPanel/cities/getList', headers=common_headers).json()['data']['cities']
cities = list(filter(lambda city: city['is_active'], cities))
cities.sort(key=lambda city: city['name'])

existing_city_names = set()
ambiguous_city_names = set()
for city in cities:
    if city['name'] in existing_city_names or city['local_name'] in existing_city_names:
        ambiguous_city_names.add(city['name'])
        ambiguous_city_names.add(city['local_name'])
    existing_city_names.add(city['name'])
    existing_city_names.add(city['local_name'])

#################### create/update city groups ####################

for city in cities:
    update_access_token()
    exists = city['id'] in city_id_to_city_group

    ideal_name = city['name']
    if city['name'] != city['local_name']:
        ideal_name = f'{city["local_name"]} ({city["name"]})'
    if city['name'] in ambiguous_city_names or city['local_name'] in ambiguous_city_names:
        # there are actually no ambigious cities (same city name in different countries),
        # except for one strange case of Valea Prahovei
        # print(f'ambiguous city name: {city["name"]} ({city["local_name"]})')
        ideal_name = f'{ideal_name} [{city["id"]}, {city["country"]}]'

    response=None
    if exists:
        city_group = city_id_to_city_group[city['id']]
        if city_group['name'] == ideal_name:
            continue # no need to update
        print(f'update {city_group["name"]} → {ideal_name}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/update',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"uuid": city_group['uuid'], "data": {"name": ideal_name, "children": [], "city_id": city['id']}})
        )
    else:
        print(f'create {ideal_name}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/create',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"data": {"name": ideal_name, "city_id": city['id'], "children": []}})
        )
    if response.status_code != 200 or response.json()['code'] != 0:
        print(f'failed to update city group {city_group["name"]} → {ideal_name}')
        print(response.json())
        exit(1)

#################### update country city groups ####################
fetch_city_groups()

country_name_to_city_group_ids = {}

def get_nice_country_name(country_name, country_code):
    emoji_flag = ''.join([chr(ord(char) + 127397) for char in country_code.upper()])
    return f'{emoji_flag} {country_name}'


for city in cities:
    city_group = city_id_to_city_group[city['id']]
    country_name = get_nice_country_name(city['country'], city['country_code'])

    if country_name not in country_name_to_city_group_ids:
        country_name_to_city_group_ids[country_name] = []
    
    country_name_to_city_group_ids[country_name].append(city_group['uuid'])

for country_name, city_group_ids in country_name_to_city_group_ids.items():
    update_access_token()
    country_name_without_flag = ' '.join(country_name.split(' ')[1:])
    if country_name in name_to_city_group or country_name_without_flag in name_to_city_group:
        city_group = name_to_city_group[country_name] if country_name in name_to_city_group else name_to_city_group[country_name_without_flag]
        if city_group['children'] == city_group_ids and city_group['name'] == country_name:
            continue # no need to update
        print(f'update {city_group["name"]}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/update',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"uuid": city_group['uuid'], "data": {"name": country_name, "children": city_group_ids, "city_id": None}})
        )
    else:
        print(f'create {country_name}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/create',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"data": {"name": country_name, "city_id": None, "children": city_group_ids}})
        )
    if response.status_code != 200 or response.json()['code'] != 0:
        print(f'failed to update country city group {country_name}')
        print(response.json())
        exit(1)

#################### update region city groups (Europe, Asia, etc.) ####################
fetch_city_groups()

region_name_to_city_group_ids = {}

for city in cities:
    country_name = get_nice_country_name(city['country'], city['country_code'])
    city_group = name_to_city_group[country_name]
    region_name = city['timezone'].split('/')[0]
    
    ### THE ONLY SPECIAL CASE: ###
    if city['country'] == 'Togo':
        region_name = 'Africa' # Togo is in Africa, but its timezone is “UTC”

    if region_name not in region_name_to_city_group_ids:
        region_name_to_city_group_ids[region_name] = []
    
    region_name_to_city_group_ids[region_name].append(city_group['uuid'])

for region_name, city_group_ids in region_name_to_city_group_ids.items():
    update_access_token()

    city_group_ids = list(set(city_group_ids))
    # sort city group ids by city group name
    city_group_ids.sort(key=lambda city_group_id: ' '.join(uuid_to_city_group[city_group_id]['name'].split(' ')[1:]))

    if region_name in name_to_city_group:
        city_group = name_to_city_group[region_name]
        if city_group['children'] == city_group_ids:
            continue # no need to update
        print(f'update {city_group["name"]}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/update',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"uuid": city_group['uuid'], "data": {"name": region_name, "children": city_group_ids, "city_id": None}})
        )
    else:
        print(f'create {region_name}')
        response = requests.post(
            f'{url}/campaign-ops-city-groups/adminPanel/cityGroup/create',
            headers=common_headers,
            data=json.dumps({"data": {"name": region_name, "city_id": None, "children": city_group_ids}})
        )
    if response.status_code != 200 or response.json()['code'] != 0:
        print(f'failed to update region city group {region_name}')
        print(response.json())
        exit(1)

There are many services calling geo-routing, but the ones that make the most calls come from rides-routing, route-prediction and route-prediction-event.

h3. geo-osrm-targeting refactoring

Reimplement endpoint receiving bulk calls, change [ModelVersionUpdate.shouldUseForward|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/d0ca38bb1a39618d094215fe49711770165e1ca0/common/models/ModelVersionUpdate.ts#L121]   to work with batches, call {{TargetingClient.safeGetBulkParamtersAsync}}

h3. route-prediction-event batching

Service already receives batched driver locations, but calls to geo-routing are fanned out at this stage. [getRoutes|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ba0140ac0a458f295b25b58590f6aab8e07dd20e/src/platform/geo/route_prediction/main/service/RouteMatcher.ts#L122C1-L148C10] and [matchPointToRoad|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/ba0140ac0a458f295b25b58590f6aab8e07dd20e/src/platform/geo/route_prediction/main/service/RouteMatcher.ts#L159C1-L166C1] endpoint calls could be batched with some effort.

h3. route-prediction batching

[getDriversLocations|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/6fab4d96c41e3019896b7db5d7a0390e4c25dfc1/src/platform/geo/route_prediction/main/service/DriverLocationService.ts#L50C1-L76C43] endpoint implementation calls [snapToRoad|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/6fab4d96c41e3019896b7db5d7a0390e4c25dfc1/src/platform/geo/route_prediction/main/service/DriverLocationService.ts#L179C1-L202C10] for out of order locations, seems low effort to batch such calls.

h3. rides-routing batching

getEtas, getEtaGroups, getEtaMatrix all call [GeoDuration.calculate|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/bab09d9c253dd54fab36ceacf7c3276ffecf68b4/src/platform/geo/delivery_routing/main/etaCalculation/GeoDurationMatrix.ts#L115C1-L142C11] that makes multiple calls to drivingDistanceMatrix, could be starting point of batching calls with some effort.

h3. Conclusion

At the time of writing the effort to refactor these services alone outshines the benefits of optimizing geo-osrm-targeting calls.

Previously we had agreed among ourselves (the fraud team and food incentives PM) that we would start by only removing discounts from bolt-provided discounts (and not provider-sided discounts). The reasoning/assumptions were that:

# Most of the providers care about volumes and not financial efficiency of the discounts. 
# We haven’t heard any case of bigger provider discounts abuse (such as food resale schemes). Except for deliberate cherrypicking behaviours such as this case. 
# Some restaurants (I don't know if its majority or minority who do this) already artificially increase their prices - e.g. case from Estonia where a popular restaurant chain has prices 10€ in-person, and 12€ in food delivery apps. So hypothesis was that they still operate at a profit even though providing big first-time-order discounts

Do you agree/disagree with this reasoning?

*Results*: By analyzing the A/B test, we saw that, even though we improved the provider viewed rate, we were hurting the overall number of orders with it. Therefore, we decided to stop the test and not rollout the feature.

*Early Hypothesis*: We think that we improved the visualization of providers, but we were showing the wrong providers - therefore the user would click on it but not order from it.

*Next Steps*: We'll wait until Selection Team to develop a new HC ranking model, ETA end of Q, to run the test again and see if we have better results.

Hey, [~accountid:5ed5e3858884020c24e9463a]! I am coming back after receiving the full feedback from the external counsel to share with you the issues that are currently blocking us from proceeding. Please review and let me know what do you think.

Issues:

# Drivers need a licence to carry out the activity. There are two options and the scope of services that fall into each licence category is not clearly defined. However, one licence allows to carry delivery services only using cars and another one allows to use other means of transport. So drivers can:
## Obtain "Freight Road Transport carried out by vehicles with a total weight of up to 3.5 t, trailer included" licence. This allows to use car only for the delivery.
## Obtain "Storage, auxiliary and transport services in transport, which also includes courier services" licence. This allows to use for the delivery  not only car (for example, scooters, bikes etc.). This licence should be more suitable for our cause.
# Important limitations for drivers: service can only be provided by cars not exceeding 3,5 t and only within the territory of Slovak Republic. 
## Action point for legal: We need to specify in T&Cs that the service is available only within the territory of SK.
# There is no requirement to have special documentation to carry out the delivery service, however, the law prescribes that a written confirmation of an order from a driver or written confirmation by the sender may be requested.
## Action point for legal: Need to set out in the T&Cs that "If special documents are required for carrying out carriage, the consignor is obliged to hand them over to the carrier no later than when handing over the consignment for carriage.".
# Undelivered parckages cannot be left at the police station. According to the local law persons providing delivery service (aka Drivers/Fleets) are required to keep parcel for 6 months from the moment when the shipment should have been delivered. After the expiry of this period they have the right to sell/dispose of it. The storage period depends on the nature of goods and their value.
# If Bolt will take responsibility to store undelivered packages, Bolt will need to obtain one of these licences: "Storage, auxiliary and transport services in transport" or "Rent of real estates and provision of other than basic rental services".

Admin panel module deployments could not be performed in parallel. This is because of the admin-panel release specifics: when the module is released, the initrc.js file is changed and uploaded to s3 to activate it. Activation happens per module. But in case of a parallel deployment, the latter release might overwrite changes introduced by the first release, making a new version of the released module unavailable.

As Kubernetes jobs run asynchronously and deployment status is validated as a part of the health check, we can not rely on the builder release locks. Release locks do not take into account health check status, which might result in a race condition explained above.

One potential solution is to extend the Lattice initrc update command with simple locking logic: before performing an update, the script will try to acquire the lock. As a lock, we will use another file in S3 (e.g. {{initrc.lock}}) with random hash and TTL. Will discuss it with admin panel owners and create a follow-up task.

Cristiana and I have been talking about this, maybe the information below will help you, a first reading of the law:

Regarding the authorization, in *GEO 34/2000* it is written in *Art 7*: "Operators and groups of operators who carry out activities of agricultural production, preparation, distribution, storage, import, export, introduction to the market of ecological products have the obligation to register this activity to the directions for agriculture of the county and of the municipality of Bucharest and to submit to the control of an approved control body." ([https://lege5.ro/App/Document/gi4dgmry/ordonanta-de-urgenta-nr-34-2000-privind-produsele-agroalimentare-ecologice).|https://lege5.ro/App/Document/gi4dgmry/ordonanta-de-urgenta-nr-34-2000-privind-produsele-agroalimentare-ecologice).]

According to *Order no. 45/2022* ([https://lege5.ro/App/Document/geydqnjrgqyde/ordinul-nr-45-2022-pentru-aprobarea-regulilor-privind-inregistrarea-activitatii-operatorilor-grupurilor-de-operatori-in-agricultura-ecologica?pid=453340151&d=2024-04-16#p-453340151|https://lege5.ro/App/Document/geydqnjrgqyde/ordinul-nr-45-2022-pentru-aprobarea-regulilor-privind-inregistrarea-activitatii-operatorilor-grupurilor-de-operatori-in-agricultura-ecologica?pid=453340151&d=2024-04-16#p-453340151|smart-link] ) Art. 2 says:
"(6) Operators/Groups of operators who sell prepackaged ECO products directly to the consumer or end user, excluding those who carry out online distribution activities, are exempt from the obligation to register in ECO agriculture, provided they declare their activity to the DAJ /DAMB and to fulfill the conditions provided for in art. 34 para. (2) of Regulation (EU) 2018/848.
(7) To benefit from the provisions of para. (6) operators/groups of operators who sell prepackaged ECO products directly to the consumer or end user, excluding those who carry out online distribution activities, submit to DAJ/DAMB in electronic format the declaration on their own responsibility for exemption from the obligation to register in organic agriculture, whose model is provided in annex no. 9.”

Regarding the above article: “_Operators/Groups of operators who sell prepackaged ECO products directly to the consumer or end user,_ *_exclusively those who carry out online distribution activities_*_, are_ *_exempt from the obligation to register in ECO agriculture_*_, provided they declare their activity at the DAJ /DAMB”._

* “exclusively those who carry out online distribution activities”. The wording is very poor, but it actually means that *online distribution* is not included in the exemption. That’s what I understand.

Because, as we can see in *Annex no. 10 (*which actually refers to operators exempt from registration), it mentions: “_The following_ *_are not exempted_* *_from registration in ECO agriculture_*_: c)_ *_operators/groups of operators that carry out online distribution activities of ECO products_*_._” Please see *Annex no 7 (registration form) i*n the Order. 

Shall we see a difference between *selling* online (putting on the market online) and *distributing* online (although I think we both sell and distribute…?). If there is such a difference, maybe we fall under *Annex 9 (*a simple *affidavit)*.

Hey, [~accountid:61d5747249f19500694358eb]! It all comes down to our risk appetite. Our template sets out our standard position which is that Landlord should insure the premises:

{quote}7.1 The Landlord shall insure the building the Premises are located at in the reinstatement value thereof at least against normal risks (fire, water, natural disasters, vandalism) and keep the respective insurance in force during the entire term of the Agreement. The Landlord shall submit the policies which evidence the compliance with the insurance obligation to Bolt at the latest within 14 days after receipt of a respective request from Bolt.
7.2 Bolt shall insure the furnishings, equipment and other assets located at the Premises and obtain the all-risk insurance at least in the reinstatement value of such assets. Bolt shall also obtain the liability insurance. Bolt shall enter into the insurance contracts specified in this clause at the latest by one month as of the time of delivery of the Premises to Bolt and, keep the respective insurances in force during the entire term of the Agreement. Bolt shall submit the policies which evidence the compliance with the insurance obligation to the Landlord at the latest within 14 days after receipt of a respective request from the Landlord.{quote}

We can take a business decision not to ask the Landlord to insure premises, but then if anything happens to the warehouse due to our fault - we will need to compensate the damage. Considering that we are going to store scooters and lithium batteries in the warehouse - our risk is quite high.

Hi [~accountid:61d5747249f19500694358eb] and [~accountid:712020:8c797c70-7a57-496e-aa3f-5d91df806eb2] 👋 



We should not insure any property that is not owned by us - please refer to this Confluence article for more context: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/cp/iJhNvPru|https://taxify.atlassian.net/l/cp/iJhNvPru|smart-link] 

In short:

* general liability policy - OK for Bolt to buy
* assets insurance (for Bolt’s property) - OK for Bolt to buy 
* (immovable) property insurance - NOT OK for Bolt to buy 

Bolt does not own the warehouse, therefore Bolt has no insurable risk to cover any damages from natural disasters, theft, and vandalism (all-risk property insurance). 

However, Bolt does realise, whilst using the warehouse, Bolt might damage the warehouse (batteries catching fire, running a scooter into a wall, a van into a gate, etc.), so Bolt should buy an insurance policy that would cover the damages that Bolt might cause (general liability policy). 

The insurance team commands the idea of insuring our own hardware and investments, however, usually, it’s been a business decision to not buy any insurance coverage, and assume the risks on our own. 



*Now, if the LL is not backing down about the all-risk property insurance, what I would suggest, is that LL will buy the insurance coverage, however the cost will be split between the LL and Bolt (and Bolt’s portion of the cost will be embedded into our rent). We should also include a clause that the landlord needs to provide the policy documents (copies) to Bolt as well (to make sure that the LL is not swindling us with the cost).* 



How other Crotian warehouse agreements have been concluded with such insurance clauses, is not clear. However, Bolt is growing and maturing, so we should try to do better now 🙂 🙏 



Best

Karmel

{code:sql}WITH first_city_order AS (					
SELECT
etl.city_id AS city_id, MIN(etl.created) AS first_order_date  				
FROM
ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
WHERE etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)			-- cities rolled OUT IN the LAST 3 months
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1
),
city_avg AS 
(
SELECT 
k.city AS city_id,
ROUND(AVG(k.count_orders),0) AS avg_city_orders 	-- 3 MONTH AVG 
FROM (
SELECT       
DATE_TRUNC('month',etl.created) AS months,
etl.city_id AS city,
etl.country_code AS country,
COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_orders
FROM
ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
WHERE etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
) AS k 
GROUP BY 1
),
country_avg AS (
SELECT 
k.country AS country,
ROUND(AVG(k.count_orders),0) AS avg_country_orders 	-- 3 MONTH AVG 
FROM (
SELECT       
DATE_TRUNC('month',etl.created) AS months,
etl.city_id AS city,
etl.country_code AS country,
COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_orders
FROM
ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
WHERE etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -3, current_date) as date)
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
) AS k 
GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
etl.city_id, 
etl.city_name, 
etl.country_code,
fco.first_order_date,
DATE_DIFF('day', fco.first_order_date, NOW()) AS date_diffs,
ca.avg_city_orders,
--coa.avg_country_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) AS count_orders,
COUNT(DISTINCT etl.driver_courier_id) AS count_active_drivers
--COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id)/ca.avg_city_orders AS against_city_avg,
--CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id)/ca.avg_city_orders >= 1 THEN 'above_city_avg' ELSE 'below_city_avg' END AS compare_to_city_avg
FROM
ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
LEFT JOIN first_city_order AS fco ON fco.city_id = etl.city_id 
LEFT JOIN city_avg AS ca ON ca.city_id = etl.city_id 
LEFT JOIN country_avg AS coa ON coa.country = etl.country_code 
WHERE etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.order_state = 'finished'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6
-- HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) < 500 OR ca.avg_city_orders < 300 OR DATE_DIFF('day', fco.first_order_date, NOW()) < 15 OR COUNT(DISTINCT etl.driver_courier_id) < 30
HAVING
COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) > 10 AND 
(
(DATE_DIFF('day', fco.first_order_date, NOW()) < 60 AND COUNT(DISTINCT etl.driver_courier_id) < 30 AND (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) < 1000 OR ca.avg_city_orders < 1000))
OR 
(DATE_DIFF('day', fco.first_order_date, NOW()) < 30 AND (COUNT(DISTINCT etl.order_id) < 500 OR COUNT(DISTINCT etl.driver_courier_id) < 30))
)
ORDER BY 5 DESC {code}

*Outgoing cases should be left* *_untagged_**.* 

The main reason for this is that usually, outgoing cases are child issues of an inbound case _(e.g., the rider lost an item, and the agent is reaching out to the driver via an outgoing case)_. The inbound case already has the tag “I lost an item“, so the linked outgoing case will technically have the same tag. Outgoing cases don’t need to be tagged, as that would create confusion with reporting. A tag to an outgoing case should be added only if the user raises a completely new issue in the ticket. 

We are aware that the information in KB on issue tagging is scattered and somewhat contradicting in some articles, but we already have a task in our backlog to look into this and fix it. I can’t give you an ETA yet, but we have it in our plans. 

Let me know if this answers your questions! 🙂
