[~accountid:620f6d352fd2470071cbafbd]  age and identity verification must be conducted before the sale of alcoholic beverages via online platforms. According to Article 6^*1*^(4) of the Alcohol Circulation Law, retailers are obligated to ensure this verification process. For Bolt Food, the restaurant authorizes Bolt to perform the verification.

Verification of identity and age must be carried out using qualified electronic identification means (Smart-ID). In theory, the restaurant remains responsible for compliance as the holder of the alcohol license. However, in practice, restaurants lack control over Bolt Food's software, making it difficult for them to ensure verification. If Bolt fails to provide technical means for compliance, we might be held jointly liable with the restaurant.

Even if the minor is ultimately denied alcohol (upon ID verification), allowing the sale could still render the restaurant and Bolt liable. This also complicates the refund process.

Therefore, implementing Smart-ID verification before online alcohol ordering is strongly recommended.

We have 2 dine-in products - Order & Pay and Pay & Go. 

* Order & Pay is a self-service QR code solution for restaurants with counter service who want to encourage customers to use QR codes to order food/drinks independently from the table (read: potential issue with age verification). 
* Pay & Go solution requires waiter to collect the order. After the food/drinks have been served and customers finished eating the food, customers can use QR code to pay for the food/drinks (read: no issue with age verification given waiter is collecting the order).

If we zoom into Order & Pay, practically it is copy paste from our pickup/takeaway flow, where customers make an order using our app and come collect the order from the location themselves. Hi [~accountid:63da287e790148a18093a774] and [~accountid:712020:8a574999-84e1-4c69-ba7b-46d08c4cff29] , I’ve reviewed the comments that Circle K had regarding the data sharing agreement.

*Speaking internally:* 

* Circle K essentially wants our roles for data processing to be joint controllers. Usually, for partnerships/promos, we consider us and partners to be independent data controllers.
* The main difference between these roles lies in liability and responsibility:
** *Joint controllers (what Circle K wants)* - Shared liability and joint responsibility for data processing.
** *Independent controllers (what Bolt wants)* - Each party is individually responsible for their data processing activities.
* We usually prefer the independent controller set-up to avoid shared liability and joint responsibility.
* The set-up exclusively depends on factual circumstances. This means that we need to clarify how data is collected and shared. 
* My goal here would be to provide an explanation to Circle K on why we consider us to be independent, and thus that no major changes to the data sharing agreement are needed.

*The most important question from me to* [~accountid:712020:8a574999-84e1-4c69-ba7b-46d08c4cff29] *is* - Are we and Circle K decisions together about how to use and process the data, or is each of us handling our own data separately? 

*Additional questions:*

* We use the following data: Drivers registered on Bolt Platform name, surname, phone numbers, email address.
* Where do we get it from? From when the driver is registering on Bolt platform?
* How do we further use it? 
* How does Circle K further use it?
* Do you have any similar partnerships to the one with Circle K?



Once we gather this information, I will draft a message to Circle K. I’d suggest not making any changes to the Data Sharing Agreement now until we agree on the role setup, because the whole agreement is dependent on it.

Hey Danil ,

In order to create base fee calculators, we would need the following information:

* *Commission rate*: Commission percentage that will apply per ride to the driver/fleet.
* *Currency*: Usually country default if not stated otherwise
* *Invoicing strategy*: Driver or Company. This will define to whom payouts will go, and invoices will be issued.
* *Booking fee:* Is there an active booking fee in the city? If so, do you want it to be deducted from the driver (and reflected on the commission invoice), or be a 100% driver income?
* *Cash-blocking thresholds*: Defines the cash ride limits for blocking/unblocking cash rides for a driver. This can be copied from other cities, but please discuss with [{color:#b3f5ff}Billing Analytics{color}|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/3/group/1240/create/806] if your market is cash-heavy.
** Max negative balance before messaging: The threshold where we will notify the driver that they are getting closer to being cash-blocked
** Max negative balance before removing cash payments: The debt threshold we allow cash rides up to. After the driver exceeds this threshold, cash orders will be disabled.
** Minimal balance to unblock cash rides: The balance threshold where we will once again unblock the driver’s cash rides.
* *List of company_ids you want this fee calculator to be attached to*.

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
*What is a Base Fee Calculator*

It is a default fee calculator template created by Billing team in order for local operations teams to easily attach the relevant fee calculator to new companies. [Please read this guide to see how|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/1603928517/Base+fee+calculators].
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Make sure to make such requests at least 3 days in advance to have buffer for gathering this information
{panel}

Hi [~accountid:5fc8dff0aca10c0069d470f1], thank you for looking into this and proposing your ideas! After careful consideration, I've concluded that implementing these suggestions wouldn’t be advisable.

* *Escalations:* We encounter many isolated cases, making it impossible to have processes for every scenario, as we can never predict what might happen to a customer (unless it's repetitive, then we create a process). It would be more effective to empower Tier1 to use their common sense when handling isolated cases rather than escalating them to Tier2. Allowing Tier1 to escalate everything that lacks a process could lead to numerous unnecessary escalations, increasing Tier2's workload and underutilizing Tier1's potential.
* *Refunds:* We have compensation guidelines approved by the Legal team and CS OPS, so Tier2 agents must adhere to our processes. While I understand that sometimes a customer who has never had issues with Bolt might receive unfair treatment, allowing Tier2 to deviate from established processes could lead to inconsistency and lack of control over our service standards.

If you’d like to discuss this further, please let me know!

Have a nice day. ☀️

Hi [~accountid:5d5a47614aeeb80c2cc0d00a] and [~accountid:6140b8db805a97006aa66cc8] 

We have now received the advice note from our external advisors on the Bolt Drovo Branding Marketing Campaign (‘Branding Campaign’).

As you may be aware when the Employment Tribunal are assessing whether an individual is an employee / worker or independent contractor they look at the practicality of the relationship between the parties that exists (in this situation the relationship between Bolt and its drivers) as opposed to what the contract may say.

If a Bolt driver decides to participate in this Branding Campaign they are required to enter into these branding terms and conditions this could be considered as a form of control as the drivers are required to complete X amount of trips to be eligible for the bonus monies. However, as drivers have the option to enter into this campaign this mitigates the risk (as drivers are not forced to enter into the campaign). In addition, the requirement that Bolt drivers need to sign a separate contract with Drovo to be eligible for the Bolt Branding Campaign introduces another layer of separation, which helps mitigate the risk.

Although the use of vehicle branding will be considered by the Employment Tribunal when assessing employment status, and branded Bolt vehicles does increase worker status risk, drivers are not required to participate in Drovo’s advertising or Bolt’s Branding Campaign. Therefore, external counsel does not view this factor as a particularly high-risk. 

*External counsel’s overall view is that this Branding Campaign and arrangement with Drovo would not be determinative of worker status, whilst it may increase the overall risk, it would not do so significantly (appreciating that this campaign also only applies to hackney cab drivers a subset of Bolts driver population).*

+*TO SUMMARISE*+ 

Essentially, the business advantages of the Branding Campaign and the commercial benefits may outweigh the increased legal risk. Provided, Bolt drivers are given the choice (as opposed to participation being mandatory)  to enter into these campaigns the risk can be mitigated against. 

Please note the termination requirements of the campaign, the campaign automatically terminates after 12 months, or it may be terminated at any time by Bolt or with 7 days’ notice from the driver.

The campaign terms and conditions to be used have been slighted amended, please ensure you are happy with the requirements outlined in clause 1.1 - [BRANDING CAMPAIGN T&CS HERE|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1m7oY-S7sH3Bc4-W_b0tjDuKcGdutzVZq/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106777530220747110658&rtpof=true&sd=true].

+*GENERAL PLATFORM TERMS: DRIVERS*+

# Acceptable Use Policy

b. You must not and you must ensure that all other Service Providers using the Bolt Platform in association with your account must not:

7(c). Not complying with the Acceptable Use Policy is a serious breach of these Terms and will entitle Bolt UK to take any of the following actions (with or without notice, subject always to Section 9):

i. immediate, temporary or permanent withdrawal of your right to use the Bolt Platform;

ii. immediate, temporary or permanent removal of any User Content;

iii. issuing a notification to you;

+*TO SUMMARISE*+

* The General Platform Terms for Drivers and the Fraud Policy (relevant sections outlined above) allow Bolt to withhold payments (these extra toll fees) from drivers if suspected fraud has occurred, therefore the business can stop paying out these extra toll charges if you are certain that these overcharges have occurred.
* It is important that when the business start withholding payments from drivers for these overcharges that drivers are allowed the right to appeal, this is outlined in Section 7(v) of the General Platform Terms for Drivers, which says:

v. withholding or permanently denying any payments payable to you as a result of prohibited behaviour that does not comply with the Fraud Policy. In these circumstances, your right to appeal such a decision is set out in the Fraud Policy;

In addition to the right to appeal outlined in section 7(v) of the General Platform Terms for Drivers, section 6 of the Fraud Policy says the following:

+*RIGHT TO APPEAL IN FRAUD POLICY*+

# Appealing a decision relating to this policy

6.1. Users will not be permitted to appeal a decision by Bolt to terminate a User’s access to the Bolt Platform in accordance with this section 6 if Bolt determines at its discretion that the failure(s) to comply with this policy are so material and/or persistant that it warrants immediate termination of a User’s access to the Bolt Platform. When this is the case, it will be made clear in the relevant Statement of Reason.

6.2. Other than in the circumstances set out in section 6.1 above, the relevant User will have 30 days from the date of issue of a Statement of Reason to appeal any decision by Bolt to suspend and/or terminate any access to the Bolt Platform in association with the User’s account. In order to appeal this decision, the relevant User must promptly appeal the decision with reference to the applicable Statement of Reason, providing Bolt with such additional Information it may request in relation to the Statement of Reason from time to time. Appeals should be made in writing and as instructed by the Statement of Reason.

6.3. Bolt will consider all appeals in good faith and will reinstate any suspended access to the Bolt Platform (and release any temporarily suspended payments to Service Providers) as soon as reasonably practicable from the date that Bolt determines at its discretion that:

6.3.1. there has not been a material failure to comply with this policy; or

6.3.2. other circumstances apply that make it fair and reasonable to reinstate access to the Bolt Platform.

6.4. If, after the expiry of the 30 day period set out in section 6.2 above, Bolt at its discretion still considers that the User has participated in (or allowed) the Prohibited Activity referred to in the Statement of Reason, Bolt will be entitled to terminate the User’s access to the Bolt Platform in accordance with the terms and conditions that apply to the User.

{color:#ff991f}*10. Contact, feedback and complaints*{color}

“_Hi __

_We wanted to confirm our current data processing setup in our partnership between Bolt and Depo._

_To be clear, Bolt operates as an independent data controller when providing services to its business customers. Our_ [+_General Terms and Conditions for Bolt Business_+|https://bolt.eu/en-th/legal/terms-for-bolt-business/?category=boltBusiness] _Section 4 states explicitly that Bolt and the business customer maintain their independent data controller roles for personal data processing. Bolt fully assumes responsibility for its processing activities and adherence to applicable laws, including the GDPR. This covers areas such as engaging subprocessors, implementing necessary security measures, and establishing data retention periods._

_When a business customer`s employee or any data subject uses Bolt Business services for a ride, they are treated as a regular user of the Bolt Rider App. The experience of these business users is identical to that of regular users, except for the availability of an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride). This may result in a scenario where, if a business customer deactivates and removes a business user's account, this individual will lose access to an alternative payment option (Bolt Business) and an additional ride category (Business Ride)._

_However, they will continue to be a customer of Bolt, which means Bolt will keep processing their personal data unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention period specified in_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/] _expires. In practical terms, this means that the personal data provided by business customers is  used to match newly added business users with the accounts of standard users. Individuals remain in control over their data._

_Additionally, as there had been a contractual relationship with the business customer, the data received from the business customer may be required for solving any dispute that may arise from the agreement with the business client. Deleting personal data on the request of business customers may deprive both Bolt and the individual from the opportunity to defend or substantiate their claims in the event that any claims should arise. Therefore, the data will be stored by Bolt as a data controller for the above stated purposes unless this individual decides to_ [+_request_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/data-subject/] _data deletion or the data retention term provided by the law (limitation period for possible claims) expires, as outlined in the applicable_ [+_Bolt`s privacy notices_+|https://bolt.eu/en/privacy/]_._

_Please note that the notion of controllership in our arrangement is cemented by the_[ |https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en][+_EDPB Guidelines 07/2020_+|https://edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-072020-concepts-controller-and-processor-gdpr_en] _on the concepts of controller and processor in the GDPR. Specifically, p. 27 para. 82 demonstrates this via “_*_Example: Taxi service”_*_. While Bolt operates as an online platform rather than providing taxi services directly, the example still effectively clarifies the logic underpinning the controller relationship._

_We appreciate your attention and trust that this explanation has clarified any concerns or questions you may have.”_

*Experiments summary*

* No duplicated IDs were found
* No performance degradations were noticed
* ID range size dynamic config works
* Note: during service shutdown (restart) we lose not only remaining IDs in current range. We also lose next range fully (next range is loaded by IMDS in advance while current range is still in use)



*Concern about losing many IDs. Will be 2^64 IDs enough for the next 20-50 years?*

Napkin estimation:

* checkpoints number = 100
* ID consumption by single checkpoint = 100B per year = 10^11 (it includes lost IDs)
* growth factor = 10
* total yearly consumption (assuming we make 10x time more checks) = 10^2 * 10^11 * 10^1 = 10^14

2^64 = (2^4)^16 = 16^16 ~ 10^16 => So, these IDs should be enough for 100 years.

*However, we assume that we don’t lose too many IDs*. We assume that services don’t restart too often (let’s say not more often than 1000 restarts per day)



*What should we do, when current ID sequence is exhausted?*

* We may start ID sequence from the beginning (it may work in case we clean all data with IDs from the beginning of sequence)
* Design different ID generation approach and migrate

Most of the stories which I see here (including the ones copied over from the duplicate epic) have very unclear goals. “So that I can have data” is a rather vague reason that doesn’t cover at all what this data is for and what action will be taken based on it. I would say that there are two ways to approach it:

# Dump all of the data somewhere and let stakeholders do whatever analysis they want with it. Looker is nice for analytics, but probably not that great if you need access to particular datapoints. The flexibility and responsibility for making sense of data is on stakeholders.
# Perform a better analysis of the needs behind the data using smth like 5 “why”s technique and tailor the solution better to the actual use cases. This requires deeper analysis and involvement, but potentially smaller involvement from stakeholders in the future (especially if it’s a one-time request).

The amount of structured data gathered from postmortems seems rather small (regardless of the way the data is collected), which makes me think that the analysis part shouldn’t become too complicated, making me lean more towards the option #1.

The artist will need our formal permission to share the song across his channels such as, but not limited to, YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok, as well as upload it to music streaming platforms such as, but not limited to, Spotify, Apple Music, and YouTube Music. Additionally, the artist can use the song as part of his live performances. The contract should probably also state that the artist is in no way representing the Bolt brand or acting as an ambassador or spokesperson.

As for music ownership, the artist and producer hold 100% ownership of the music rights, the license, and thereby its subsequent royalties. The artist and producer are responsible for registering the song according to local laws and for publishing the song via a record label of their choice or as independent artists.

Since Bolt holds no part of the license, Bolt is not in a position to use the song in its own materials. However, Bolt is still allowed to talk about and promote the song wherever found suitable.

clause 3.4. of T&C for Client stipulate that:

 *_“_**The Client must comply with applicable laws,* including the requirements applicable upon *purchase of alcohol,* tobacco, energy drinks or any other products requiring age verification. In case the Client wants to order products requiring *age verification, he/she must confirm and/or prove his/her age as part of the ordering process.* Further, the Delivery Partner delivering the Order and/or the Partner in case of self pick-up by the Client, Order and Pay or Pay and Go *may refuse to hand over the products requiring age verification, if the Client does not present a valid photo identification proving that he/she is old enough* to legally purchase the products or if the Client shows signs of intoxication. # *how do we handle situation when under age buys alcohol via takeaway service and is denied to provide alcohol by the restaurant on pickup?* 
#  *Does restaurant reimburse the difference to the customer?* 
# *Does restaurant have the right to withhold the amount of money received from selling alcohol to a customer that was confirmed under age?*



The process is mapped and described by the KB team [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539] (_I will copy below in case you cannot access Beehive)_ 





*_COPY_*_:_ 

🥡🥕 Eater did not present ID or was underage

Providers with the _Alcohol_ policy can sell alcoholic beverages on the platform. If the eater chooses the:

* [_Delivery_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF5096T4C3WQV39S9AA8YN] [option|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF5096T4C3WQV39S9AA8YN], the courier will [verify their age when making the delivery|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/public/360020738859].
* [_Pickup_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF57JB5F3HPBWPAGE9ZQBN][/|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF57JB5F3HPBWPAGE9ZQBN][_Takeaway_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF57JB5F3HPBWPAGE9ZQBN] [option|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360015833539#h_01G5GF57JB5F3HPBWPAGE9ZQBN], the provider’s staff needs to check the eater's age at the collection point.

*Important!* The person who made the order has to provide the ID. If they are underage or unable to verify their age, they should not be given the age-restricted items, regardless of if there is another person over the legal age with them. 

----

h3. *Delivery order*

The courier must check the eater's ID and then tick the _Verify the client’s age_ box in the app:

*Eater is above the legal age*

* The courier can deliver the order

*Eater is below the legal age/does not have ID*

* The courier can only deliver non-alcoholic items
* Advise the courier to dispose of the alcoholic items (applicable to all markets)
* If the order was a Bolt Market order and the value of the alcoholic item(s) is more than half the order value, advise the courier to dispose of the order. Do not refund the customer.

----

h3. *Pickup order*

There is currently no in-app prompt or app feature guiding restaurant staff to do this but this is advised in the provider onboarding process.

In the event that the restaurant is not able to verify the eater’s age (the eater did not have an ID or they are confirmed to be underage), inform the staff of the following details:

* They should not give the alcohol to the eater, only non-alcohol items are to be handed over
* The alcohol items can be restocked by the restaurant as the eater is not eligible for a refund in these cases.

{quote}*Additional Information for cash orders*

* Most providers have opted in to only receive cashless pickup orders i.e. the order is already paid when placing the order:
** If the customer is not given their alcohol item(s), they are not eligible for a refund (please check your local [Bolt Food Legal|https://food.bolt.eu/en-us/] page for the specific term).
* If the provider is contacting us about a cash pick up where the customer does not want to pay the full amount or didn’t pay at all, follow the steps below:
** If the order is still active, manually _Succeed_the order then add a note with a link to the Beehive case in the eater's account.
** If the provider clicked the _Received_ amount:
*** Ask them to follow their own restaurant no payment policy to reconcile the amount off their earnings
*** Request a deduction for the commission charged for the order. Find the _Manual Adjustment Sheet_ for your market in the [Useful Links|https://bolt.eu/en/support/articles/360008083419/] article.{quote}
